newsitem.title: CHINA: Storms hit HK, disrupt handover carnival, traffic.
newsitem.headline: Storms hit HK, disrupt handover carnival, traffic.

text.p: Thunderstorms lashed Hong Kong on Wednesday, flooding some areas and spoiling a carnival parade to celebrate the former British colony's reunion with China.
Floods disrupted traffic and kept people off the streets on the final day of a five-day holiday to mark Hong Kong's handover at midnight on Monday. Eight people were injured in a landslip.

Floats representing animals and Chinese themes stood soggily on a central waterfront promenade as organisers cancelled the procession. A limited parade later made its way to the city's Victoria Park, but the foul weather reduced the crowds.
Rescue teams searched for a woman trapped in her home under a landslip after the torrential rain.
Train services were severely disrupted on the Kowloon Canton Railway because of landslips on the track and hundreds of passengers were forced to take shuttle buses.
Shatin in the New Territories was the worst hit. Severe flooding there submerged cars in muddy water in some carparks and rescue divers were called in to check if anyone was trapped.
Sub-tropical Hong Kong's rainy season starts around late June and runs through September, and many handover-related activities have been rained on during the past few days.
